content.text:
I read the structure in pieces and then joined them.

**Left side.** A pyridin-2-yl ring carries an N-Boc nitrogen, N(Boc)(pyridin-2-yl). A propyl chain (three CH2) links this nitrogen to N1 of an indazole.

**Indazole.** N1 bears the propyl chain and N2 is the adjacent ring nitrogen. C3 is the CH at the top (drawn as N=CH). The benzene ring is fused at C3a/C7a. The amide carbonyl sits at C5, which is para to C7a... in the drawing it is at the top of the benzene ring, adjacent to C3a. So C5 is attached to C4, which is attached to C3a. Indazole SMILES: n1(CCC...)c2ccc(C(=O)N...)cc2cn1 — here C7a is bonded to N1, then C7, C6, C5 (carrying the amide), C4, C3a, C3, N2. This matches the drawing.

**Amino acid part.** The amide NH connects to CH2, then to CH(NH-SO2Ar), then to C(=O)OMe. The stereocentre is drawn with a bold wedge to the ester carbon. This is a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid derivative; I assume the S configuration, as in L-Dap.

For the SMILES I write the stereocentre as N[C@@H](CNC(=O)...)C(=O)OC and check the chirality. With the neighbours in the order N, H, CH2, COOMe, "@@" means that, looking from N, the sequence H, CH2, COOMe runs clockwise.

CIP priorities are N > COOMe > CH2N > H. Look from N with H, CH2, C(=O) clockwise. The same chirality can be written as [C@@H] with neighbours in the order (N, H, CH2, CO). Swapping to put H as the viewing atom: the order N, H, CH2, CO has H as the second neighbour, so I use a permutation. Moving H to the front takes one swap, giving H, N, CH2, CO with the chirality flipped to "@". Looking from H, N → CH2 → CO is anticlockwise. Seen from the opposite side (H pointing away), it is clockwise: N → CH2 → CO. The priority order N → CO → CH2 is the reverse of that, so it is anticlockwise, which gives S. So N[C@@H](CN...)C(=O)OC is S, which is what I want.

**Aryl sulfonyl.** The sulfonyl group is on a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring with a 4-alkoxy substituent. The alkoxy chain is O-CH2CH2CH2-C(=O)NH-CH2CH2NH2.

**Full SMILES:**
CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N(CCCn1ncc2cc(C(=O)NC[C@H](NS(=O)(=O)c3c(C)cc(OCCCC(=O)NCCN)cc3C)C(=O)OC)ccc21)c1ccccn1

Here I wrote the stereocentre as C[C@H](N...)C(=O)OC, with the preceding atom being CH2. Neighbours in order: CH2, H, N, CO. Relative to N, H, CH2, CO (@@), the new order CH2, H, N, CO swaps N and CH2, which is one swap, so the symbol flips to @@ → @. So [C@H] is correct.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N(CCCn1ncc2cc(C(=O)NC[C@H](NS(=O)(=O)c3c(C)cc(OCCCC(=O)NCCN)cc3C)C(=O)OC)ccc21)c1ccccn1
